question: After a climate event, when will a credible damage figure exist, and who will publish it?
note: Every entry is assembled from estimators' own published schedules and observed practice. No entry states what an event will cost. The 'settles' field is DERIVED from the sequence and is therefore Combined under D-033, not Compiled; it must render with the Combined label.

basis_values.published_schedule: the estimator publishes this timing itself; a commitment
basis_values.observed_practice: not published as a schedule, inferred from repeated behaviour
basis_values.conditional: happens only if triggered, for example on request or above a threshold

entries.label: European windstorm
entries.coverage_note: The densest early coverage of any hazard and territory in this map, because PERILS commits to dated restatements.

worked_example.note: Up then down, total movement about 2.5 percent. A stable estimate is information; a ledger that showed only the current figure would hide it.

absence_meaning.note: PERILS publishes nothing below EUR 300 million in a single country or EUR 500 million pan-European. The threshold is published and the estimator was watching, so silence here is weak evidence the event fell below it.

entries.label: US wildfire, hurricane and severe convective storm

sequence.label: PCS preliminary, resurveyed every 60 days above USD 250 M
added to the billion-dollar series once assessed
December preliminary, then sigma 1 in Q1

settles.label: sigma in the Q1 following the event year

entries.coverage_note: The fastest figures here are the least documented. AccuWeather publishes within a day with no methodology; the documented estimators take months.

worked_example.note: AccuWeather's three figures are dated to January 2025 only; exact dates are unverified and must not be published until confirmed. The event was ongoing across all three, so the rise mixes event growth with knowledge growth.

absence_meaning.note: PCS resurveys only above USD 250 million, and the billion-dollar series is billion-dollar by definition. Silence is weak evidence the event fell below those thresholds, not evidence of nothing.

entries.label: Australian bushfire and cyclone
entries.coverage_note: PERILS covers Australia, so the schedule is as dated as Europe's.

absence_meaning.note: PERILS covers both the peril and the territory here. Its Australian reporting threshold is not verified in this map, so treat silence as unexplained until it is.

entries.label: Indonesian fire and haze

sequence.label: national agency (BNPB) figures
sequence.note: not yet profiled; needs its own estimator record before use

sequence.label: EM-DAT entry, revised as sources report

settles.label: no settled figure expected within the event year; the 2015 season was still being re-estimated in 2021

entries.coverage_note: No insured-loss index covers Indonesian wildfire. The authoritative figures arrive years later and disagree; see the 2015 decomposition.

figures.note: Published as a country economic analysis, not a GRADE assessment. Includes USD 3.97 bn carbon valuation. Eight provinces.

worked_example.note: Six years between the two figures. Decomposed, the land-cover components agree within about 2 percent and the gap is the social cost of carbon plus long-term mortality valuation.

absence_meaning.note: No insured-loss index covers Indonesian wildfire. Silence says nothing whatsoever about the size of the event.

entries.label: Southern Africa drought

sequence.label: SADC / OCHA appeals
sequence.note: an appeal is a funding request, NOT a loss; separate category, never summed with damage

settles.label: often never, as a money figure

entries.coverage_note: Slow-onset drought has no event end date, so no schedule anchored on one can apply. The humanitarian system produces caseloads and appeals rather than loss estimates. This is the hardest hazard in the map and the honest answer is that a damage figure may never arrive.

absence_meaning.note: No estimator produces damage figures for slow-onset drought here. The humanitarian system produces appeals, which measure response scale rather than loss. Silence says nothing about size.

entries.label: Coastal Peru and Ecuador flooding

settles.label: years; the 1982-83 event is still cited from EM-DAT in 2017 dollars

entries.coverage_note: GRADE is the fastest credible option here and it is conditional on being requested, so its absence is not evidence of a small event.

absence_meaning.note: GRADE is produced on request rather than automatically, so its absence is not evidence of a small event.

entries.label: Mediterranean wildfire (France, Spain, Portugal, Greece)

sequence.label: national schemes: Consorcio de Compensacion de Seguros (Spain), CCR (France)
sequence.note: not yet profiled; these are the likeliest first insured figures for this hazard and territory and should be the next estimators added

settles.label: no scheduled settlement; the quarterly recaps are the only dated commitments

entries.coverage_note: PERILS covers NEITHER the peril nor several of the territories. Its European perils are windstorm, flood, hail and convective storm, plus earthquake in Italy and Turkey; wildfire is not among them. Its European country list is Austria, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Switzerland and the UK, so Spain, Portugal and Greece are outside it entirely. Australian bushfire is covered; Mediterranean wildfire is not.
entries.editorial_note: This matters more than a coverage gap usually would. The France and Spain fires of July 2026 are T4's worked example of the fast-reaction thesis, and they sit in a hole: no scheduled insured-loss estimator covers them, so the first credible figure will come from national schemes with no published timetable. The site's flagship speed argument lands on the hazard where the money data is slowest.

absence_meaning.note: PERILS covers neither wildfire as a European peril nor Spain, Portugal and Greece as territories. Silence says nothing about size.

absence_reason_values.below_threshold: an estimator was watching and publishes a threshold; silence is weak evidence the event fell below it
absence_reason_values.outside_coverage: no estimator covers this hazard and territory; silence says nothing about size
absence_reason_values.not_yet_valid: a reading exists but is before its earliest valid point and can be confidently wrong; treated as absent

absence_note: A missing figure is never rendered as a small figure. These three absences read identically on a page and mean opposite things.
